description: Use AI image to video to add gentle motion to a product photo you already like. Download a short clip for Reels, TikTok, or your shop. Upload a shot to start.
h1: Turn a Product Photo Into Motion With AI Image to Video
lead: AI image to video turns a product shot you already like into a short clip. Add a slow camera move, drifting light, or steam rising from a cup, and download it in the size you need.
intro: Image to video takes one still photo of your product and adds movement to it. The camera can push in slowly, circle the item, or pan across a table, while light, water, fabric, or steam moves around it. Because it starts from your photo, the clip stays close to the look you already chose: the same product, colors, and setting.

It suits sellers who have a strong product photo but no moving version yet. Use it for product galleries, Reels, Stories, or feed placements. Set the movement to 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, then choose 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

benefits.d: There's no new shoot to plan. The photo on your product page right now can be the starting point for a video.
Ask for small moves like a slow zoom or a light sweep. Gentle motion keeps attention on the product instead of the effect.
Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. The shortest option is handy for Reels and Stories, where clips replay on their own.

steps.d: Pick a sharp image with some space around the product so the camera has room to move.
Write one line about the movement, like “slow push-in while morning light moves across the bottle,” then choose the length and size.
Keep the clip you like. If the movement feels too fast, rewrite your line and run it once more.

uses.d: Add the clip to your Shopify product gallery so shoppers see a little movement among the still photos.
Post a vertical video based on an ad photo that already does well for you.
Swap a still feed ad for a square moving version of the same image.
A wide 16:9 clip with slow motion makes a calm header at the top of your shop.

faq.q: What kind of photo works for image to video?
faq.a: A sharp, well-lit photo with the product fully in frame. Leave some background around it, because tight crops give the camera nowhere to go.

faq.q: Can I choose how the camera moves?
faq.a: Yes, describe it in your sentence. Phrases like “slow zoom in,” “orbit around the bottle,” or “pan left across the table” give the clearest direction. Motion can vary between runs, so a second try may land closer to what you pictured.

faq.q: Will my product look exactly like the photo?
faq.a: It stays close, but fine details like small printed text, buttons, or label lettering can shift once things move. Watch the clip all the way through before posting it, and run it again if something looks off.

faq.q: Can I make several clips from the same photo?
faq.a: Yes. Each run makes one clip, so change the motion or size and run it again. The credit cost is shown for every run before it starts.

overview.h2: Animate the photograph you already approved
overview.p: Image to video is useful when the product photo is right but a still frame feels too quiet. Keep the product, palette, and setting as the visual anchor, then describe one movement that adds life around it.

overview.h2: Ask for one kind of motion at a time
overview.p: A camera push, a slow pan, drifting steam, moving water, or a sweep of light each gives the model a clear job. Combining several large effects makes it harder to tell whether the product itself stayed accurate.

input_guide.h2: Give the camera a stable starting frame

items.d: Use a frame that includes the complete object and its most important edges, handles, openings, or attachments.
A margin around the item gives a push or pan space to travel without clipping the product.
For glass, metal, or glossy packaging, start with a highlight that does not hide the label or main shape.
Use a background with enough contrast behind clear lids, bottles, or lenses so their outline remains readable as the scene moves.
Write one direction such as “slow push toward the bottle while morning light crosses the table,” rather than listing several unrelated actions.
Select 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and receive one clip for each run.
Use 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 when you need a particular frame.
The workspace shows the credit amount before it runs, and a failed job returns those credits.
The download has no watermark and can be reviewed for a product page, social post, or ad before you publish it.

after_download.h2: Check the moving details before posting

items.t: Compare the first and last frame
items.d: Confirm the silhouette, color, cap, clasp, or printed panel still matches the approved photo.
Type product names, prices, dates, and captions in your editing or publishing tool instead of relying on generated lettering.
If a second run changes the product less or keeps the camera steadier, use that version for the final placement.

fit.h2: Best matches for image to video
good: Hero photos with space around a single product
Objects where light, steam, water, or fabric can move around the item
Product galleries that need one moving frame among still images
Brands testing a subtle visual opening before planning a larger shoot
not_ideal: Photos packed edge to edge with no room for a camera move
Scenes where tiny labels or exact small text must remain unchanged
